![BarPlan logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zmann85/BarPlan/main/logo.svg)

# BarPlan

**Your action bars as a plan: set up every new character of a class the same way, spells you haven't learned yet included.**

A WoW Forever addon.

[**⬇️ Download the latest version**](https://github.com/zmann85/BarPlan/releases/latest)  ·  [What's new](https://github.com/zmann85/BarPlan/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Install
1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/zmann85/BarPlan/releases/latest) and download the `BarPlan-…zip` file under **Assets**.
2. Unzip it into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\` (you should end up with an `AddOns\BarPlan` folder).
3. Start the game or type `/reload`.

To update, repeat this and replace the old folder. Your plans are kept.

## What it does
Your action bars as a plan. Set up one character's bars the way you like them, save them as a named plan, and
a new character of that class gets the same bars, including the spells it hasn't learned yet. Each spell goes onto its
button the moment you learn it, and a new rank replaces the old one on the same button.

No placeholder macros needed: a spell button waits empty until you learn the spell. A macro that only casts one
spell (`#showtooltip X` / `/cast X`) is saved as that spell, so you can keep such placeholders on the character
you save from (for spells it can't learn yet) and new characters get the plain spell. Macros with logic in them
(stance swaps, mouseover, /startattack) are part of the plan too and are made on the new character when it
doesn't have them.

## Use

`/barplan` or the minimap button opens the window.

1. **Save your bars:** on a character whose bars are done, type a name (default: your class) and click Save.
   Plans belong to the class they were saved on: a warrior's plans are only offered to warriors.
2. **On a new character** of that class, BarPlan asks at the first login, with your class's plans in a dropdown
   (the one marked for new characters chosen). Or pick one in the window and click Apply (twice: it clears the
   buttons the plan has empty). What you know goes on now, the rest as you learn it.
3. **Play.** Learned spells go onto their buttons (after the fight when you learn one in combat).

**Addons too.** A plan keeps which addons were on when you saved it. Applying it switches this character's addons
to match and offers a reload, since the game only loads or unloads addons then. Addons you installed after saving
the plan are left as they are, and addons the plan had on but you don't have installed are listed. A plan saved
before BarPlan 1.4 has no addon list: save it again on its character to add one.

**Chat tabs too.** A plan keeps your chat tabs: each tab's name, which message types and channels it shows, its
font size, colour and place in the dock. Applying it sets General and Combat Log up the same, opens the tabs you
added (matched by name), and closes added tabs the plan doesn't have. Where the chat window sits stays as it is.

**Keybindings too.** A plan saved on a character with its own keybindings (the "character specific" box in the
game's keybinding options) keeps every key and what it does, macros and addon buttons included. Applying it
gives the new character those keys as its own set. A plan saved on a character using the account-wide keys
keeps those keys too: applying it makes the new character use the account-wide keys and sets them to the plan's,
so a new account or a fresh WoW folder gets your keys as well.
The window also has a **Character specific keybindings** switch that shows and changes it for the character
you're on, like the box in the game's keybinding options: on gives it its own set (a copy of the keys it has
now), off goes back to the account-wide keys.

**Edit Mode layout too.** A plan keeps the Blizzard Edit Mode layout its character uses. Applying it adds that
layout (replacing an older one of the same name) and makes it the new character's, set up at the reload BarPlan
offers.

All four are on by default; each has an On/Off switch in the window (or `/barplan addons on|off`, `/barplan chat
on|off`, `/barplan keys on|off`, `/barplan editmode on|off`). Plans always save all four, so you can switch them on later.

**Share plans.** The window's plan list shows the plans of every class (yours first), so you can export any of
them from any character; Apply stays for your own class. Export (or `/barplan export [name]`) gives the chosen
plan as a text string to keep or send on, Export all (`/barplan exportall`) every plan in one string; Import
(`/barplan import`) adds what a string holds, each plan to its class, on any character or account. A name you
already have gets a number ("Paladin (2)"), so nothing is replaced by accident. Macros that run code (`/run`,
`/script`, `/console`, `/click` ...) are left out of an imported plan by default, so its buttons can only cast,
use, target or say things; a checkbox in the import window takes them in too, if you trust the text.

In the window you can also pick which plan new characters of your class are offered, delete a plan, and switch
off putting learned spells on the bars for this character.

A button you empty yourself after BarPlan filled it stays empty, and a button you put something else on stays
yours. A spell the plan keeps at a lower rank (you had a lower rank on that button when saving) stays at that
rank.

## Commands

| Command | |
|---|---|
| `/barplan` | the window |
| `/barplan save [name]` | save this character's bars as a plan of its class |
| `/barplan apply [name]` | set this character's bars up from a plan of its class |
| `/barplan status` | the plan this character follows and the spells still to learn |
| `/barplan list` | your class's plans |
| `/barplan use <name>` | the plan new characters of your class are offered |
| `/barplan delete <name>` | delete a plan of your class |
| `/barplan off` / `on` | stop / resume putting learned spells on the bars |
| `/barplan addons on` / `off` | whether Apply also switches your addons |
| `/barplan chat on` / `off` | whether Apply also sets up your chat tabs |
| `/barplan keys on` / `off` | whether Apply also sets up your keybindings |
| `/barplan editmode on` / `off` | whether Apply also sets up your Edit Mode layout |
| `/barplan export [name]` / `exportall` / `import` | share a plan (or all) as text / add from text |
| `/barplan debug [from-to]` | what BarPlan sees on those buttons (default 1-12), for bug reports |
| `/barplan minimap` | hide / show the minimap button (also a checkbox in the window) |

`/bplan` works too.

## Notes

- Plans live in `WTF\Account\<account>\SavedVariables\BarPlan.lua`. Copy that file to take your plans to
  another WoW folder or account.
- Character macros are limited to 30 by the game; a plan macro that doesn't fit is reported, not made.

## Third-party parts

Embedded in `libs/` for the minimap button, each under its own license:
- LibStub - public domain.
- CallbackHandler-1.0 - Ace3 Development Team, BSD license (libs/CallbackHandler-1.0/LICENSE.txt).
- LibDataBroker-1.1 - tekkub.
- LibDBIcon-1.0 - funkydude, Ace3-style BSD license.
- LibDeflate - Haoqian He, zlib license (libs/LibDeflate/LICENSE.txt).
- LibSerialize - Ross Nichols, MIT license (libs/LibSerialize/LICENSE).

# Changelog

## v1.11.3 (2026-10-23)

### Fixed
- A macro like `/cast !Stealth` was saved as a spell called "!Stealth", so its button stayed empty on a new
  character. A "!" in front (it keeps Stealth, an aura or a stance from toggling off) now keeps it a macro. A plan
  saved before puts the macro back on that button when applied.

## v1.11.2 (2026-10-23)

### Fixed
- Apply from the window could freeze the game for a moment when it changed many keybindings: the window redrew
  itself once for every key. It now redraws once.
- Export and Export all took noticeably long with several plans. They use a faster compression setting now (the text
  is a little longer; Import reads both).
- After the Import window had been open, Export showed Import's summary and its "macros that run code" checkbox under
  the text. It shows the character count again.

## v1.11.1 (2026-10-21)

### Fixed
- A button BarPlan couldn't read when a plan was saved was left out of the plan, so Apply cleared it and put
  nothing back. Such a button is now kept in the plan as "keep as it is", and Apply leaves it alone.

### New
- `/barplan debug [from-to]` (default 1-12) lists what BarPlan sees on those buttons and what the plan has there,
  for bug reports.

## v1.11.0 (2026-10-21)

### New
- The plan list in the window shows the plans of every class (yours first, each with its class), so you can
  export, delete or choose the plan offered to new characters of any class from any character. Apply stays for
  plans of your own class. `/barplan export <name>` finds a plan of another class by its name too.
- Export all (in the window, or `/barplan exportall`): every plan of every class in one text. Import adds them
  all back.
- Import no longer replaces a plan by default: a name you already have gets a number ("Paladin (2)"). The window
  says for each plan what will happen; for a single plan you can still type an existing name to replace it.
- Macros that run code are still left out of an imported plan by default; a checkbox in the import window (shown
  when the text has such macros, off each time) imports them too, at your own discretion.

## v1.10.1 (2026-10-21)

### Fixed
- The reload question after Apply could sit behind or overlap other windows. It now stays in front of everything,
  in the middle of the screen.

## v1.10.0 (2026-10-20)

### New
- Share a plan as a text string: Export in the window (or `/barplan export [name]`) shows it to copy; Import
  (`/barplan import`) adds a plan from one to its class, on any character or account. Macros that run code
  (`/run`, `/script`, `/console`, `/click` ...) are left out of an imported plan.

## v1.9.1 (2026-10-20)

### Fixed
- A spell you learn was left where the game put it, on the first empty button: on a button the plan keeps for a
  spell you haven't learned yet (which then never went there), or on one the plan keeps empty. A spell the game
  places as you learn it now goes off any button the plan doesn't have it on, so the plan's buttons stay free.

## v1.9.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Edit Mode layout: a plan keeps the Blizzard Edit Mode layout its character uses. Applying it adds the layout
  (replacing an older one of the same name), makes it the new character's and offers a reload to set it up.
  Its own On/Off switch in the window, `/barplan editmode on|off`. Save a plan again to add its layout.
- The reload question after Apply covers addons and the layout together.

## v1.8.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- A plan saved on a character using the account-wide keybindings now keeps those keys too. Applying it sets the
  account-wide keys to the plan's, so a new account or a fresh WoW folder gets your keys as well (before, it only
  switched the character to the account-wide keys, whatever they were). Save such a plan again to add its keys.

## v1.7.0 (2026-10-19)

First release on CurseForge.

### New
- A macro that only casts one spell (`#showtooltip X` / `/cast X`) is saved in a plan as that spell. Keep such
  placeholders on the character you save from (for spells it can't learn yet): new characters get the plain
  spell on that button when they learn it, and no macro.

## v1.6.1 (2026-10-19)

### New
- "Character specific keybindings" switch in the window: shows whether the character you're on has its own
  keybindings and turns them on (a copy of your current keys) or off (back to the account-wide keys).

## v1.6.0 (2026-10-19)

### New

  spell and addon button keys included). Applying it gives the new character those keys as its own set; a plan
  saved with the account-wide keys gives it the account-wide keys.
- `/barplan keys on|off`.

## v1.5.2 (2026-10-19)

### Fixed
- Which addons are on was read wrongly when several of your characters share a name (deleted and made again):
  every addon counted as on, so a plan's addon list didn't switch anything. Addons are now read and switched
  for exactly the character you're on.

## v1.5.1 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Addons, chat tabs (and from v1.6 keybindings) each have an On/Off switch in the window, on by default:
  whether Apply sets them up too. `/barplan addons on|off`, `/barplan chat on|off`.

## v1.5.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Chat tabs: a plan keeps each chat tab's name, message types, channels, font size, colour and place in the
  dock. Applying it sets General and Combat Log up the same, opens the tabs you added and closes added tabs the
  plan doesn't have.

## v1.4.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Addons: a plan keeps which addons were on. Applying it switches this character's addons to match and offers
  a reload.

## v1.3.1 and earlier

- Save a character's action bars as a named plan of its class; a new character of that class is offered the
  plan at its first login. Spells you haven't learned yet go onto their buttons when you learn them, a new rank

  spell and addon button keys included). Applying it gives the new character those keys as its own set; a plan
  saved with the account-wide keys gives it the account-wide keys.
- `/barplan keys on|off`.

## v1.5.2 (2026-10-19)

### Fixed
- Which addons are on was read wrongly when several of your characters share a name (deleted and made again):
  every addon counted as on, so a plan's addon list didn't switch anything. Addons are now read and switched
  for exactly the character you're on.

## v1.5.1 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Addons, chat tabs (and from v1.6 keybindings) each have an On/Off switch in the window, on by default:
  whether Apply sets them up too. `/barplan addons on|off`, `/barplan chat on|off`.

## v1.5.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Chat tabs: a plan keeps each chat tab's name, message types, channels, font size, colour and place in the
  dock. Applying it sets General and Combat Log up the same, opens the tabs you added and closes added tabs the
  plan doesn't have.

## v1.4.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Addons: a plan keeps which addons were on. Applying it switches this character's addons to match and offers
  a reload.

## v1.3.1 and earlier

- Save a character's action bars as a named plan of its class; a new character of that class is offered the
  plan at its first login. Spells you haven't learned yet go onto their buttons when you learn them, a new rank
  replaces the old one, and macros of the plan are made when missing. Minimap button and `/barplan` window.

# Changelog

## v1.10.1 (2026-10-21)

### Fixed
- The reload question after Apply could sit behind or overlap other windows. It now stays in front of everything,
  in the middle of the screen.

## v1.10.0 (2026-10-20)

### New
- Share a plan as a text string: Export in the window (or `/barplan export [name]`) shows it to copy; Import
  (`/barplan import`) adds a plan from one to its class, on any character or account. Macros that run code
  (`/run`, `/script`, `/console`, `/click` ...) are left out of an imported plan.

## v1.9.1 (2026-10-20)

### Fixed
- A spell you learn was left where the game put it, on the first empty button: on a button the plan keeps for a
  spell you haven't learned yet (which then never went there), or on one the plan keeps empty. A spell the game
  places as you learn it now goes off any button the plan doesn't have it on, so the plan's buttons stay free.

## v1.9.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- Edit Mode layout: a plan keeps the Blizzard Edit Mode layout its character uses. Applying it adds the layout
  (replacing an older one of the same name), makes it the new character's and offers a reload to set it up.
  Its own On/Off switch in the window, `/barplan editmode on|off`. Save a plan again to add its layout.
- The reload question after Apply covers addons and the layout together.

## v1.8.0 (2026-10-19)

### New
- A plan saved on a character using the account-wide keybindings now keeps those keys too. Applying it sets the
  account-wide keys to the plan's, so a new account or a fresh WoW folder gets your keys as well (before, it only
  switched the character to the account-wide keys, whatever they were). Save such a plan again to add its keys.
